peanuts.name: Peanuts
peanuts.note: Good source of protein and healthy fats. Watch portion size.

profile_notes.infants: Peanuts — allergy risk, introduce carefully under guidance

palm_oil.name: Palm oil
palm_oil.note: High in saturated fat. Linked to raised LDL cholesterol. Very commonly used in Indian snacks.

profile_notes.infants: Palm oil — not suitable for infants

sugar.name: Sugar
sugar.note: Added sugar with no nutritional benefit. Common hidden in 'healthy' products.

profile_notes.infants: Sugar — not suitable under 2 years
profile_notes.fitness: Sugar — empty calories, causes fat storage

salt.name: Salt
salt.note: Small amounts fine. Indians typically consume 2-3x the safe daily limit already.

profile_notes.infants: Salt — infant kidneys cannot process sodium

wheat_flour.name: Wheat flour (maida)
wheat_flour.note: Refined flour — stripped of fibre and nutrients, spikes blood sugar. Whole wheat atta is better.

profile_notes.diabetics: Maida — high glycemic index, raises blood glucose fast
profile_notes.infants: Wheat — gluten may cause issues in young infants

whole_wheat_flour.name: Whole wheat flour
whole_wheat_flour.note: Much better than refined flour. Retains fibre, vitamins, and minerals.

profile_notes.infants: Wheat — contains gluten, avoid under 6 months
profile_notes.diabetics: Whole wheat — better than maida but still watch portions

rice_flour.name: Rice flour
rice_flour.note: Gluten-free. High glycemic index — spikes blood sugar similarly to refined flour.

profile_notes.diabetics: Rice flour — high GI, raises blood glucose

milk_solids.name: Milk solids
milk_solids.note: Good source of calcium and protein.

profile_notes.infants: Milk solids — not a substitute for breast milk

hydrogenated_fat.name: Hydrogenated fat (vanaspati)
hydrogenated_fat.note: Trans fats. Strongly linked to heart disease. No safe level of consumption.

profile_notes.adults: Trans fat — raises bad cholesterol, lowers good cholesterol
profile_notes.fitness: Trans fat — interferes with cell function

soy_lecithin.name: Soy lecithin (322)
soy_lecithin.note: Common emulsifier, generally safe. Soy allergen for some people.

profile_notes.infants: Soy lecithin — soy allergy risk

e471.name: Emulsifier (471)
e471.note: Keeps texture smooth. Source often animal fat or palm-derived. Generally safe in small amounts.

profile_notes.infants: E471 — source unclear, avoid in infants

emulsifier_472e.name: Emulsifier (472e)
emulsifier_472e.note: Dough strengthener from fatty acids. Generally safe.

profile_notes.infants: 472e — avoid additive-heavy foods in infants

maltodextrin.name: Maltodextrin
maltodextrin.note: Processed filler starch with GI higher than table sugar. Spikes blood glucose fast.

profile_notes.diabetics: Maltodextrin — GI of 110, spikes blood sugar faster than sugar
profile_notes.infants: Maltodextrin — ultra-processed, avoid for infants
profile_notes.fitness: Maltodextrin — causes energy crash after spike

malt_extract.name: Malt extract
malt_extract.note: Natural sweetener from barley. Contains gluten. Raises blood sugar.

profile_notes.infants: Malt extract — gluten content, avoid under 6 months

tocopherol.name: Antioxidant (307 / vitamin E)
tocopherol.note: Natural antioxidant — vitamin E. Used to prevent rancidity in oils. Safe for all.

sulphite_223.name: Dough conditioner / preservative (223)
sulphite_223.note: Can trigger asthma and allergic reactions in sulphite-sensitive people. A declared allergen.

profile_notes.infants: Sulphite 223 — allergic reactions in children

raising_agent_503.name: Raising agent (503)
raising_agent_503.note: Leavening agent for biscuits/cakes. Breaks down completely during baking — safe.

profile_notes.infants: Raising agents — avoid additive-heavy processed foods for infants

raising_agent_500.name: Raising agent (500 / baking soda)
raising_agent_500.note: Common baking soda. Safe in food amounts.

profile_notes.hypertension: Sodium bicarbonate — adds to sodium intake

maltitol.name: Sweetener — maltitol (965)
maltitol.note: Sugar alcohol. Still raises blood sugar. Causes bloating and digestive distress in larger amounts.

profile_notes.diabetics: Maltitol — raises blood sugar unlike other sugar alcohols
profile_notes.infants: Sweeteners — not suitable under 2 years

sucralose.name: Sweetener — sucralose (955)
sucralose.note: 600x sweeter than sugar. Long-term effects still studied. Disrupts gut bacteria in some research.

profile_notes.infants: Sucralose — artificial sweeteners not suitable for infants
profile_notes.pregnant: Sucralose — limited safety data in pregnancy

acesulfame_k.name: Sweetener — acesulfame-K (950)
acesulfame_k.note: Artificial sweetener often paired with sucralose. Passes through body unchanged. Long-term safety debated.

profile_notes.infants: Artificial sweeteners — not suitable for infants
profile_notes.pregnant: Acesulfame-K — limited safety data, best avoided

aspartame.name: Sweetener — aspartame (951)
aspartame.note: Contains phenylalanine — dangerous for people with PKU. WHO classified as 'possibly carcinogenic' in 2023.

profile_notes.pregnant: Aspartame — WHO classified as possible carcinogen in 2023, avoid
profile_notes.infants: Aspartame — not suitable, contains phenylalanine
profile_notes.adults: Aspartame — WHO 2023 review raised cancer concerns at high intake

stevia.name: Sweetener — stevia (960)
stevia.note: Plant-derived natural sweetener. Does not raise blood sugar. One of the safer sweeteners.

profile_notes.infants: Stevia — not well studied in very young children

msg.name: MSG / flavour enhancer (621)
msg.note: Common in chips, instant noodles, snack mixes. Some people report headaches and nausea. Regulated but not banned in India.

profile_notes.infants: MSG — not suitable for infants
profile_notes.elderly: MSG — linked to headaches and sensitivity reactions

ins_635.name: Flavour enhancer (635)
ins_635.note: Used with MSG for stronger flavour. Brands use it to claim 'No MSG' while getting same effect. Gout risk.

profile_notes.infants: 635 — not suitable for infants

tartrazine.name: Food colour — tartrazine (102)
tartrazine.note: Synthetic yellow dye. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Banned in some countries. Watch for in candies, chips, and drinks.

profile_notes.infants: Tartrazine — linked to hyperactivity and allergies in children
profile_notes.pregnant: Tartrazine — avoid artificial dyes during pregnancy

sunset_yellow.name: Food colour — sunset yellow (110)
sunset_yellow.note: Synthetic orange dye. Linked to hyperactivity. Banned in Norway. Common in Indian sweets and drinks.

profile_notes.infants: Sunset yellow — linked to behavioural issues in children

caramel_colour.name: Caramel colour (150)
caramel_colour.note: Type 150d (used in colas) contains 4-MEI — a potential carcinogen. Common in sauces, soy sauce, colas, baked goods.

profile_notes.infants: Caramel colour — avoid artificial additives for infants
profile_notes.pregnant: Caramel 150d — potential carcinogen, limit cola consumption

sodium_benzoate.name: Preservative — sodium benzoate (211)
sodium_benzoate.note: Reacts with vitamin C to form benzene — a known carcinogen. Common in juices and soft drinks.

profile_notes.infants: 211 — linked to hyperactivity in children

potassium_sorbate.name: Preservative — potassium sorbate (202)
potassium_sorbate.note: Common preservative in bread, cheese, juices. Generally safe at food levels.

profile_notes.infants: Preservatives — avoid processed foods for infants

citric_acid.name: Acidity regulator — citric acid (330)
citric_acid.note: Naturally found in citrus fruits. Safe. Adds sour taste and acts as preservative.

ascorbic_acid.name: Vitamin C / antioxidant (300)
ascorbic_acid.note: Vitamin C — natural antioxidant. Safe and beneficial. Caution: reacts with sodium benzoate (211) to form benzene.

bha_bht.name: Antioxidant BHA/BHT (320/321)
bha_bht.note: Synthetic antioxidants. BHA (320) classified as possible carcinogen. Common in chips, fried snacks, packaged nuts.

profile_notes.infants: BHA/BHT — synthetic chemicals, avoid in children
profile_notes.pregnant: BHA — possible carcinogen, avoid during pregnancy

tbhq.name: Antioxidant TBHQ (319)
tbhq.note: Synthetic antioxidant. Very common in Indian fried snacks and biscuits. Linked to DNA damage in high doses.

profile_notes.infants: TBHQ — avoid synthetic antioxidants for infants
profile_notes.pregnant: TBHQ — linked to cell damage, avoid during pregnancy
profile_notes.adults: TBHQ — safe at regulated levels but cumulative exposure is a concern

guar_gum.name: Thickener — guar gum (412)
guar_gum.note: Natural plant-based thickener and fibre source. Safe. Actually good for digestion.

xanthan_gum.name: Thickener — xanthan gum (415)
xanthan_gum.note: Fermentation-derived thickener. Safe for most people. Can cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

profile_notes.infants: Xanthan gum — linked to necrotising enterocolitis in premature infants

carrageenan.name: Thickener — carrageenan (407)
carrageenan.note: Seaweed-derived thickener. Common in dairy drinks and ice cream. Linked to gut inflammation in some studies.

profile_notes.infants: Carrageenan — linked to gut inflammation, avoid in infant foods

cocoa.name: Cocoa
cocoa.note: Rich in antioxidants. Good in moderation. Usually paired with lots of sugar in packaged products.

profile_notes.infants: Cocoa — contains caffeine, avoid under 2 years
profile_notes.diabetics: Cocoa — pure cocoa is fine, watch added sugar alongside

raising_503.name: Raising agent (503)
raising_503.note: Leavening agent — breaks down completely during baking. Safe.

profile_notes.infants: Raising agents — avoid additive-heavy processed foods for infants

raising_500.name: Raising agent (500 / baking soda)
raising_500.note: Common baking soda. Safe in food amounts.

profile_notes.hypertension: Sodium bicarbonate — adds to daily sodium intake

sulphite.name: Preservative / dough conditioner (223 / 221)
sulphite.note: Can trigger asthma and allergic reactions. A declared allergen on Indian labels.

profile_notes.infants: Sulphite — allergic reactions in sensitive children

artificial_flavouring.name: Artificial flavouring
artificial_flavouring.note: Synthetic flavour chemicals. Exact composition often undisclosed on label.

profile_notes.infants: Artificial flavouring — not suitable for infants
profile_notes.pregnant: Artificial flavouring — undisclosed chemicals, best avoided

wheat_bran.name: Wheat bran
wheat_bran.note: High in fibre. Great for digestion and blood sugar control. Contains gluten.

profile_notes.infants: Wheat bran — gluten content, avoid under 6 months

spice.name: Spices
spice.note: Natural spices. Generally safe and anti-inflammatory.

profile_notes.infants: Spices — may irritate infant digestive system

corn.name: Corn / maize
corn.note: Common base for chips and snacks. High starch content.

profile_notes.diabetics: Corn — moderate glycemic index, watch portions

potato.name: Potato / potato starch
potato.note: Natural vegetable. High glycemic index especially when fried.

profile_notes.diabetics: Potato — high GI, spikes blood sugar especially when fried

soy_protein.name: Soy protein / soya
soy_protein.note: Good plant protein source. Allergen for some. Contains phytoestrogens.

profile_notes.infants: Soy — top allergen, introduce carefully

vegetable_fat.name: Vegetable fat / shortening
vegetable_fat.note: Vague label — could be palm oil, coconut oil, or partially hydrogenated fat. Ask for source.

profile_notes.adults: Vegetable fat — source matters hugely; palm = saturated, hydrogenated = trans fat

coconut_oil.name: Coconut oil
coconut_oil.note: High in saturated fat but a different type than palm oil. Better than vanaspati. Use in moderation.

profile_notes.hypertension: Coconut oil — high saturated fat, watch total intake

groundnut_oil.name: Groundnut oil (peanut oil)
groundnut_oil.note: One of the healthier oils used in Indian snacks. Rich in monounsaturated fats.

profile_notes.infants: Groundnut oil — peanut allergy risk

sesame_seeds.name: Sesame seeds / til
sesame_seeds.note: Good source of calcium and healthy fats. Allergen for some.

profile_notes.infants: Sesame — allergen, introduce carefully

oats.name: Oats
oats.note: Excellent source of soluble fibre. Lowers cholesterol. Good for blood sugar control.

profile_notes.infants: Oats — introduce carefully after 6 months

milk.name: Milk
milk.note: Good source of calcium, protein, and vitamins. Dairy allergen for some.

profile_notes.infants: Cow's milk — not suitable as main drink before 1 year

butter.name: Butter
butter.note: Natural dairy fat. High in saturated fat. Better than vanaspati but use in moderation.

profile_notes.hypertension: Butter — saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol

ghee.name: Ghee (clarified butter)
ghee.note: Traditional Indian fat. Rich in fat-soluble vitamins. High in saturated fat — use in moderation.

acidity_regulator_330.name: Acidity regulator (330 / citric acid)
acidity_regulator_330.note: Safe. Found naturally in citrus. Used in juices, candies, and chips.

tamarind.name: Tamarind
tamarind.note: Natural souring agent. Rich in antioxidants. Safe.

profile_notes.infants: Tamarind — sour taste, may not suit infants

mango_pulp.name: Mango pulp / fruit pulp
mango_pulp.note: Natural but concentrated — high in natural sugars. Much better than artificial flavouring.

profile_notes.diabetics: Fruit concentrate — high natural sugar, still raises blood glucose

inulin.name: Inulin / chicory fibre
inulin.note: Prebiotic fibre. Feeds good gut bacteria. May cause bloating in large amounts.

profile_notes.infants: Inulin — prebiotic fibre not needed for infants

sunflower_oil.name: Sunflower oil
sunflower_oil.note: One of the healthier cooking oils. Rich in vitamin E and linoleic acid.

mustard_oil.name: Mustard oil
mustard_oil.note: Traditional Indian oil. Good fat profile. Some concern about erucic acid in very large quantities.

profile_notes.infants: Mustard oil — strong flavour and erucic acid content, introduce carefully

lentils.name: Lentils / dal
lentils.note: Excellent source of plant protein and fibre. Low glycemic index.

chickpeas.name: Chickpeas / besan
chickpeas.note: Excellent plant protein and fibre source. Low glycemic index. Good for blood sugar control.

sodium_phosphate.name: Phosphate additive (339 / 450 / 451)
sodium_phosphate.note: Common in processed cheese, instant noodles. Excess phosphate linked to kidney stress and bone density loss.

profile_notes.infants: Phosphates — avoid in infants
profile_notes.elderly: Phosphates — excess linked to kidney and bone issues

tapioca_starch.name: Tapioca starch / sabudana
tapioca_starch.note: Gluten-free starch. High glycemic index. Often used as filler.

profile_notes.diabetics: Tapioca — high GI, raises blood glucose fast

whey_protein.name: Whey protein
whey_protein.note: High quality dairy protein. Excellent for muscle building and satiety.

profile_notes.infants: Whey — not suitable as main protein source for infants

water.name: Water
water.note: Plain water. Zero calories, zero concern.

glycerol.name: Glycerol / glycerin (422)
glycerol.note: Keeps food moist. Derived from plant or animal fats. Safe at food levels. Slightly sweet.

profile_notes.diabetics: Glycerol — metabolises like a carbohydrate, adds small amount of calories

rapeseed_oil.name: Rapeseed oil (canola)
rapeseed_oil.note: One of the healthiest cooking oils. Low in saturated fat, high in omega-3. Good choice.

sodium_hydrogen_carbonate.name: Raising agent — sodium hydrogen carbonate (500)
sodium_hydrogen_carbonate.note: Common leavening agent. Breaks down during baking. Safe in food amounts.

profile_notes.hypertension: Sodium bicarbonate — adds to daily sodium intake

egg.name: Egg / egg solids
egg.note: Excellent source of protein, vitamins D and B12. Allergen for some people.

profile_notes.infants: Egg — top allergen, introduce carefully after 6 months

diglycerides.name: Diglycerides of fatty acids (471)
aliases: mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
diglycerides.note: Emulsifier derived from fats (often palm or animal). Keeps texture smooth. Source often undisclosed.

profile_notes.infants: Diglycerides — source unclear, avoid in infant foods

olive_oil.name: Olive oil
olive_oil.note: One of the healthiest oils. Rich in monounsaturated fats and antioxidants.

starch.name: Starch / modified starch
starch.note: Used as thickener or filler. High glycemic index. Often highly processed.

profile_notes.diabetics: Modified starch — raises blood sugar, similar to maltodextrin

vinegar.name: Vinegar / acetic acid
vinegar.note: Natural preservative. Safe. May even help with blood sugar control.

yeast.name: Yeast / yeast extract
yeast.note: Natural leavening or flavour agent. Rich in B vitamins. Safe for most people.

skimmed_milk.name: Skimmed milk
skimmed_milk.note: Low-fat dairy. Good protein and calcium source. Less saturated fat than whole milk.

profile_notes.infants: Cow's milk — not suitable as main drink before 1 year

cream.name: Cream
cream.note: High in saturated fat. Use in moderation.

profile_notes.hypertension: Cream — high saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.note: Good protein and calcium source but high in saturated fat and sodium.

profile_notes.infants: Cheese — high salt, not for infants under 1 year

tomato.name: Tomato / tomato paste
tomato.note: Rich in lycopene and vitamin C. Natural and beneficial.

onion.name: Onion / onion powder
onion.note: Natural ingredient. Anti-inflammatory. Safe for all.

profile_notes.infants: Onion — strong flavour, may cause gas in infants

garlic.name: Garlic / garlic powder
garlic.note: Natural antibacterial properties. Beneficial for heart health.

profile_notes.infants: Garlic — strong flavour, introduce carefully

sodium_citrate.name: Acidity regulator — sodium citrate (331)
sodium_citrate.note: Salt of citric acid. Safe. Used to control acidity in juices and dairy.

profile_notes.hypertension: Sodium citrate — adds sodium, watch total daily intake

calcium_carbonate.name: Calcium carbonate (170)
calcium_carbonate.note: Natural calcium source. Used as anticaking agent or acidity regulator. Safe.

iron.name: Iron (fortification)
iron.note: Added iron for nutritional fortification. Beneficial especially for women and children.

zinc.name: Zinc (fortification)
zinc.note: Added zinc for immune function. Safe at fortification levels.

niacin.name: Niacin / vitamin B3
niacin.note: B vitamin. Essential for energy metabolism. Safe at fortification levels.

riboflavin.name: Riboflavin / vitamin B2 (101)
riboflavin.note: B vitamin. Also used as a natural yellow food colour. Safe.

folic_acid.name: Folic acid / vitamin B9
folic_acid.note: Essential B vitamin. Especially important during pregnancy for neural tube development.

vitamin_d.name: Vitamin D
vitamin_d.note: Essential fat-soluble vitamin for bone health and immunity.

pectin.name: Pectin (440)
pectin.note: Natural fibre from fruit peels. Used as gelling agent in jams and jelly. Beneficial for gut health.

agar.name: Agar / agar-agar (406)
agar.note: Seaweed-derived gelling agent. Vegan alternative to gelatin. Safe.

gelatin.name: Gelatin
gelatin.note: Derived from animal bones/skin. Not vegan or vegetarian. Halal/Kosher status depends on source.

profile_notes.infants: Gelatin — source unclear, check if suitable

dextrose.name: Dextrose / glucose
dextrose.note: Pure glucose — the fastest-absorbing sugar. Spikes blood glucose immediately.

profile_notes.diabetics: Dextrose — pure glucose, spikes blood sugar faster than sugar
profile_notes.infants: Dextrose — added sugars not suitable under 2 years

fructose.name: Fructose (fruit sugar)
fructose.note: Processed entirely by the liver. Excess linked to fatty liver and high triglycerides.

profile_notes.diabetics: Fructose — processed in liver, linked to fatty liver in excess
profile_notes.infants: Fructose — added sugars not suitable under 2 years

sorbitol.name: Sorbitol (420)
sorbitol.note: Sugar alcohol. Causes laxative effect in large quantities. Lower GI than sugar.

profile_notes.infants: Sorbitol — not suitable for infants
profile_notes.elderly: Sorbitol — laxative effect at higher doses

sunflower_lecithin.name: Sunflower lecithin
sunflower_lecithin.note: Plant-based emulsifier from sunflower. Good alternative to soy lecithin. Safe.

potassium_chloride.name: Potassium chloride (508)
potassium_chloride.note: Used as salt substitute or firming agent. Generally safe. Excess can affect kidneys.

profile_notes.infants: Potassium chloride — not suitable for infant kidneys
profile_notes.elderly: Potassium chloride — excess can stress kidneys

lactic_acid.name: Lactic acid (270)
lactic_acid.note: Natural acid found in fermented foods. Safe. Produced by gut bacteria naturally.

malic_acid.name: Malic acid (296)
malic_acid.note: Natural acid found in apples. Safe as food additive.

annatto.name: Annatto / bixin (160b)
annatto.note: Natural orange-yellow dye from annatto seeds. Can cause allergic reactions in some people.

profile_notes.infants: Annatto — can cause allergic reactions, avoid in infants

curcumin.name: Turmeric / curcumin (100)
curcumin.note: Natural yellow colour from turmeric. Anti-inflammatory. Safe and beneficial.

beta_carotene.name: Beta-carotene / vitamin A (160a)
beta_carotene.note: Natural orange pigment and precursor to vitamin A. Safe and nutritious.

silicon_dioxide.name: Anticaking agent — silicon dioxide (551)
silicon_dioxide.note: Prevents clumping in powdered foods. Long-term effects of inhaled silica are dangerous but food-grade ingestion is generally considered safe.

profile_notes.infants: Anticaking agents — avoid in infant foods

magnesium_stearate.name: Magnesium stearate (572)
magnesium_stearate.note: Anticaking or release agent. Generally safe in food amounts.

profile_notes.infants: Anticaking agents — avoid in infant foods

natural_flavour.name: Natural flavouring
natural_flavour.note: Derived from natural sources but exact composition often undisclosed. Better than artificial.

profile_notes.infants: Natural flavouring — exact source unclear, introduce carefully

iodine.name: Iodine (fortification)
iodine.note: Essential mineral for thyroid function. Safe at fortification levels.
